reviews.review:
Girls and Quiz is a compact casual title that combines trivia questions with the presentation and character-focused appeal of a visual novel. Developed and published by morojenoe's empire, it is built around a straightforward idea: meet a group of anime-style girls, answer their questions, and see what happens depending on how well you perform. It does not attempt to compete with larger visual novels in terms of storytelling depth or production values, but its unusual mixture of quiz mechanics and character interactions gives it a distinctive identity.

The main attraction is the trivia system. Instead of progressing almost entirely through dialogue, players repeatedly answer questions associated with the different characters. Correct answers naturally move the experience toward favorable results, although deliberately making mistakes can also be useful when exploring alternative outcomes or pursuing achievements. This gives the otherwise simple question-and-answer structure a little more flexibility, particularly for completion-oriented players who want to experience everything available rather than simply aiming for perfect scores.

Four girls provide the central character component, with each acting as more than a decorative backdrop for the trivia. Their presence gives the quizzes a light dating-show or game-show atmosphere, while the visual novel presentation provides short interactions surrounding the questions. The protagonist can also be personalized with a chosen name, helping the experience feel slightly more direct. Character development is fairly limited, however, and anyone expecting lengthy romance routes, emotional storytelling, or complicated relationship systems should keep expectations modest.

The game contains a considerable number of questions relative to its small scope, with roughly 200 trivia questions forming the foundation of the experience. That quantity helps extend the concept beyond a handful of quick rounds, although variety ultimately depends more on the questions themselves than on mechanical changes. The basic activity remains largely unchanged from beginning to end, so players who do not enjoy trivia are unlikely to find enough additional systems to maintain their interest.

Achievement hunting adds another layer of motivation. There are 14 Steam achievements, providing goals beyond simply finishing a single playthrough. Some encourage players to experiment with different results and character interactions, making repeated attempts more meaningful. Because the overall structure is uncomplicated, revisiting the game to clean up missing achievements is relatively painless. This makes it particularly suitable for players who enjoy smaller Steam titles that can be completed without a massive investment of time.

Presentation is deliberately modest. Anime-inspired character illustrations carry much of the visual appeal, while the interface concentrates on dialogue and question selection rather than animation or cinematic effects. The style works adequately for the game's purpose, but environments and presentation elements are fairly restrained. Players accustomed to highly polished visual novels with elaborate character animation, extensive backgrounds, or professional voice acting may find the package sparse.

Audio follows the same minimalist philosophy. Music supplies atmosphere during the quiz sessions, but there is no extensive full voice performance driving the character interactions. Since reading is central to both the story portions and the trivia itself, the experience feels closer to an interactive quiz book presented through a visual novel interface than a fully produced narrative adventure. Language support includes English, Simplified Chinese, Russian, and Japanese for interface and subtitle content, making the game accessible to several different audiences.

One of the more interesting aspects is how naturally the two genres complement each other despite their simplicity. Visual novels can sometimes become passive when interaction is limited to occasionally selecting dialogue choices, while trivia games can feel sterile when questions are presented without personality or context. Girls and Quiz places characters around the trivia, giving players a reason to care about their results while keeping them actively involved. The implementation is basic, but the concept itself is charming enough to distinguish the game from completely conventional trivia releases.

Its limitations become clearer during longer sessions. There is little mechanical evolution, the narrative material is lightweight, and the characters do not receive enough development to create the attachment expected from more substantial visual novels. Repetition can therefore settle in quickly. The experience works better in short sessions where a few rounds of questions remain entertaining rather than attempting to play through everything continuously.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially listed with a Verified or Playable rating on the Steam store. The game was designed as a Windows title, so Steam Deck users should consider its compatibility unofficial. Given its lightweight visual novel and menu-based design, it may be possible to run through Proton, but players should not treat native or officially validated Steam Deck support as guaranteed. Controls may also require touchscreen, trackpad, or custom controller configuration depending on how the interface behaves.

Overall, Girls and Quiz is best approached as a small experimental combination of visual novel presentation and casual trivia rather than a deep representative of either genre. Its approximately 200 questions, multiple characters, achievements, and alternate results create enough material for several short sessions, while the uncomplicated structure makes it accessible from the outset. The tradeoff is limited storytelling, repetitive mechanics, minimal production complexity, and no official Steam Deck verification. For trivia fans and achievement hunters who enjoy anime aesthetics, it can still provide a pleasantly unusual distraction.

Rating: 5/10
